answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by making every identity pay: an agent locks a deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fakes means locking a thousand deposits, and a fraud proof slashes the whole bond, turning the attack into a cost spiral that grows faster than any gain. Reputation then acts as a bridge between the locked stake and future work: honest agents keep their bond and earn the nectar of fees, while a fake that burns its bond once cannot cheaply return.
